messages:
dmitri: Quick follow-up from the private-controlplane RFC — need decision on connectivity pattern.

Options:
A) VPC Peering / Transit Gateway (Redwood hosts peered CP endpoints in our account)
B) Reverse-initiated TLS connector (customer VPC runs outbound agent that opens TLS to Redwood)

Primary concerns: compliance (no inbound), egress costs, route management, cert lifecycle, multi-region failover, and support surface.

Questions: which do we prefer as default for new Private customers, and when to recommend hybrid?

sally: For B, how do we do cert rotation? ACME? KMS-signed proxy certs? Who owns the signing keys?

ben: Peering costs: TGW attachments + route table scaling. Also cross-account peering gets messy with many customers.

alice: Egress NAT costs are real for reverse-TLS. For high throughput customers peering might be cheaper even with TGW fees.

carla: Compliance note — some customers forbid inbound connections entirely. Reverse-TLS is necessary for them (agent must be customer-managed).

mike: Proposal: default = connector (Reverse-TLS) for first pass. Offer peering/TGW as 'high-throughput' paid option. Hybrid: long-lived peering with connector as fallback.
Example agent config snippet:
```
CONNECTOR_AGENT=
  mode=outbound
  target=cp.redwood.example.com:443
  cert_kms_alias=projects/redwood/kms/connector-signing
  auth_token=REDACTED
  health_check=/healthz
```

infra-bot: note: connector requires NAT egress & static egress IP if customers want allowlist. See runbook: https://internal/redwood/connector-runbook 

dmitri: Rollout plan: pilot w/ 2 customers (one compliance-only low throughput, one high throughput), measure egress cost delta + control-plane latency. Canary: 10% of new private signups use peering for 3 months.
Metrics to collect: control_plane_p99_latency, connector_dial_success_rate, egress_cost_per_month, route_convergence_time.

sally: Also add atomic audit log replication requirement — signed envelopes from connector agent forwarded to S3 in customer account.

ben: DNS: private hosted zone vs mTLS SNI routing — choose SNI-based routing to avoid needing route53 delegation complexity.

carla: Support impact: connector means we need a 'connector diagnostics' tool that can collect agent logs, CRs, and network traces via customer opt-in.

dmitri: Action items:
- mike draft connector design doc w/ cert lifecycle + restart semantics
- infra: estimate TGW cost model for 100/1k/5k customers
- sally: audit replication sketch
We'll sync on Mon arch sync. Thanks :thumbsup:
